what: Vorv's own build toolchain: a Java runtime, the Android API jar, the dexer and the signer.
why: Turning source into an installable app needs javac, d8 and apksigner, all of which are Java. A phone has no Java, so it travels inside the app.

sdkFiles.why: the Android API javac compiles against, and d8 links against
signs the finished apk so Android will install it

note: Nothing here is committed: 200 MB of binaries would make the repository unclonable. Rebuild them with tools/forge/fetch-runtime.sh. No Termux app, no Termux runtime and no Termux path is installed or needed; these are the same open-source builds, carried by Vorv and started from its own native library directory.

linuxSystem.what: The Linux system Vorv runs: proot plus a Debian 12 (bookworm) arm64 root filesystem.
linuxSystem.why: proot runs an unprivileged userland by interposing on syscalls, so the guest sees a root filesystem that is really a folder in Vorv's storage. Debian, not Alpine, because Android's build tools are glibc binaries: Debian ships aapt, zipalign, apksigner and openjdk-17 for arm64 natively (research: docs/research/linux-choice.md). Alpine's musl cannot run them.

rootfs.name: debian-12-bookworm-arm64-slim
rootfs.note: Stored as gzipped tar (28 MB) named rootfs.tar, because AGP strips a .gz suffix off asset names; the extractor sniffs the gzip magic. Assembled from the official debian:bookworm-slim arm64 layer with every blob checked against its registry sha256.

toolchain.what: The Android build tools: openjdk-17 (javac/java), aapt, zipalign, apksigner and every library they link against, fetched once on first setup and unpacked into the guest. Payloads are Debian .deb archives, each checked against the sha256 apt published for it.
toolchain.where: On the phone, at run time — 203 MB of .deb files is too much to ship inside the APK.
toolchain.resolvedClosure: tools/forge/toolchain-packages.json lists the full apt-resolved closure (169 packages) that these came from.

mavenFiles.why: the Kotlin compiler itself, so self-repair can compile a patch on the phone without Termux
kotlin.* has to resolve on the target classpath; kotlinc runs with -no-stdlib
org.jetbrains.annotations, referenced by the stdlib's signatures
